title: Matthew 25:1-12 | Excerpt from "The Negro Bible: The Making Of A Slave"

sense.text:
“Then shall the kingdom of heaven be likened unto ten virgins, which took their lamps, and went forth to meet the bridegroom.” Ten virgins. Now we know who the virgins are: the 144,000 of the twelve tribes of Israel, the elect of God, espoused to one husband.

“Which took their lamps.” The commandment is the lamp and the law is the light, so these ten took the commandments and their understanding with them and went out to meet the bridegroom.

And the Lord says of these virgins, “Turn, O backsliding children, saith the Lord; for I am married unto you.”

precepts.why:
Here is the precept to identify these virgins. Paul says, “For I am jealous over you with godly jealousy: for I have espoused you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.”

So Paul is presenting us as a chaste virgin to Christ. The virgins are not ten women waiting on a wedding; they are the people the Most High has espoused to one husband.

That is where the parable starts: Israel, espoused to Christ, waiting on the bridegroom.

Pay attention to this one. “And I looked, and, lo, a Lamb stood on the mount Sion, and with him an hundred forty and four thousand, having his Father’s name written in their foreheads.” The Father’s name written in their foreheads, because the Lord is going to give us the name of the Father.

Read on. “And I heard a voice from heaven, as the voice of many waters, and as the voice of a great thunder: and I heard the voice of harpers harping with their harps: And they sung as it were a new song before the throne, and before the four beasts, and the elders: and no man could learn that song but the hundred and forty and four thousand, which were redeemed from the earth.” No man could learn that song. These are the leaders.

“These are they which were not defiled with women; for they are virgins.” The 144 is not going to make the mistake Adam made and follow philosophies from his wife. Not defiled with women is talking about philosophy. “These are they which follow the Lamb whithersoever he goeth” — meaning they ain’t going to make excuses. “These were redeemed from among men, being the firstfruits unto God and to the Lamb.” These are men; the 144 is not women.

So now we know who the virgins are. It is talking about the 144,000 of the twelve tribes of Israel.

To quickly identify who the 144,000 is, go to the seventh chapter. “And I heard the number of them which were sealed: and there were sealed an hundred and forty and four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel.”

Of all the tribes of the children of Israel. Y’all see that right there? You got the Jehovah Witness tower saying the 144 is in there, and people believe that crap. Are you kidding me? The number sealed is sealed out of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel, and nobody else.

Now go back to the fourteenth chapter and read it again with that: the hundred forty and four thousand standing with the Lamb on the mount Sion, with the Father’s name in their foreheads, are Israelites.

We are still dealing with the virgins. “Go and proclaim these words toward the north, and say, Return, thou backsliding Israel, saith the Lord; and I will not cause mine anger to fall upon you: for I am merciful, saith the Lord, and I will not keep anger for ever.”

“Only acknowledge thine iniquity.” That is what the Lord requires of us: acknowledge the wrongs we’ve done, our sins. “That thou hast transgressed against the Lord thy God, and hast scattered thy ways to the strangers under every green tree, and ye have not obeyed my voice, saith the Lord.”

Here is the part we want. “Turn, O backsliding children, saith the Lord; for I am married unto you.” I am married unto you. “And I will take you one of a city, and two of a family, and I will bring you to Zion.” So he ain’t getting all Israel: one of a city and two of a family, and he will bring them to Zion.

“Which took their lamps.” What is the lamp? “For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light; and reproofs of instruction are the way of life.”

The commandment is a lamp and the law of God is light. So these ten virgins, who represent the elect of God, took their lamps: they took the commandments and their understanding.

sense.text:
“And five of them were wise, and five were foolish.” Right there you have the wise and the foolish to identify.

The measure is the commandments. You want to know if you’re wise? Are you keeping the commandments? The foolish ain’t going to be keeping the commandments.

precepts.why:
“The wise in heart will receive commandments: but a prating fool shall fall.”

That is the difference between the five wise and the five foolish. The wise in heart receive commandments. The prating fool falls, meaning they ain’t going to be keeping the commandments.

So right there you have the wise and the foolish identified. Are you keeping the commandments, or are you a prating fool?

sense.text:
“They that were foolish took their lamps, and took no oil with them: But the wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps.” The foolish took no oil with them. The wise took oil in their vessels with their lamps: understanding with the commandments.

The lamp is the commandment and the law. The oil is the understanding.

“While the bridegroom tarried, they all slumbered and slept.” All ten of them, the wise and the foolish alike.

What it means that we slumbered and slept is that we would lose our heritage. We have forgotten who we are.

“And at midnight there was a cry made, Behold, the bridegroom cometh; go ye out to meet him.” So time is passing now. At midnight the cry is made and the virgins are called out to meet him.

And you can’t read the New Testament without reading the Old Testament; you’ll be lost. The Old Testament says what that midnight cry is.

precepts.why:
What does it mean we slumbered and slept? “And thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee; and I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not: for ye have kindled a fire in mine anger, which shall burn for ever.”

So we would discontinue from our heritage, and we would be made to serve our enemies in a land we knew not. That is what it means. We slumbered and slept: we lost our heritage and we have forgotten who we are.

We just read it, but this is what the cry at midnight is talking about. “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the Lord: And he shall turn the heart of the fathers to the children, and the heart of the children to their fathers, lest I come and smite the earth with a curse.”

So “Behold, the bridegroom cometh; go ye out to meet him” is the cry that goes out before the great and dreadful day of the Lord, and it turns the heart of the fathers to the children and the heart of the children to their fathers.

That is why you can’t read the New Testament without reading the Old Testament. You’ll be lost.

sense.text:
“Then all those virgins arose, and trimmed their lamps.” They all rose up and trimmed their lamps.

Remember it said they all slumbered and slept. This is the waking up: arise out of that dead state and trim the lamp again.

precepts.why:
“Wherefore he saith, Awake thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall give thee light.” Remember it said we all slumbered and slept. So now it is saying awake thou that sleepest. Arise from that dead state you’re in, and Christ shall give thee light.

Read on. “See then that ye walk circumspectly, not as fools, but as wise, Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.” Not as fools, but as wise. There are the fools and the wise again. Redeeming the time, because the days are evil.

That is what it is for all those virgins to arise and trim their lamps: awake out of the sleep, arise from the dead, and walk as wise and not as fools.

sense.text:
“And the foolish said unto the wise, Give us of your oil; for our lamps are gone out.” The foolish wanted the oil of the wise. I pray I’m part of that.

Their lamps are gone out because they wasted it. Yeah, we wasted it.

precepts.why:
“There is treasure to be desired and oil in the dwelling of the wise; but a foolish man spendeth it up.”

Oil in the dwelling of the wise. See that? But a foolish man spendeth it up. You don’t regard it.

sense.text:
“But the wise answered, saying, Not so; lest there be not enough for us and you: but go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves.” The wise cannot hand over their oil; there would not be enough for us and you. The foolish are sent to buy for themselves.

And where you go to buy is the Lord. You got to go to the Lord; only the Lord can help you.

precepts.why:
Let’s see what “go ye rather to them that sell, and buy for yourselves” is talking about. “Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters, and he that hath no money; come ye, buy, and eat; yea, come, buy wine and milk without money and without price.”

Come ye to the waters. He that hath no money, come ye buy and eat — buy wine and milk without money and without price. And the next verse: “Wherefore do ye spend money for that which is not bread? and your labour for that which satisfieth not? hearken diligently unto me.” See that that “me” is the Lord.

So you got to go to the Lord. Only the Lord can give you that understanding, only the Lord can enlighten your eyes, only the Lord can bring salvation. We can’t do it. Man can’t do it.

Remember we read earlier, go to them that sell and buy. Here is a precept for that. Christ said what? “I counsel thee to buy of me gold tried in the fire.” I counsel thee to buy of me. That is why you got to go to the Lord: go to them that sell and buy, and you got to go to the Lord.

“That thou mayest be rich; and white raiment, that thou mayest be clothed, and that the shame of thy nakedness do not appear” — meaning the shame of your sin do not appear. You want it to be forgiven.

“And anoint thine eyes with eyesalve, that thou mayest see.” See that part right there. Anoint your eyes with the eyesalve, so that your spiritual eyes can see.

sense.text:
“And while they went to buy, the bridegroom came; and they that were ready went in with him to the marriage: and the door was shut.” While they went to buy, the bridegroom came.

The ones that were ready went in with him to the marriage, and the door was shut. Uh-oh.
“Afterward came also the other virgins, saying, Lord, Lord, open to us.” That is the five foolish, on the outside of a shut door, saying Lord, Lord, open to us.

“But he answered and said, Verily I say unto you, I know you not.” I know you not.

They called him Lord, Lord, and they are told he never knew them, because they were not doing the will of the Father, and the will of the Father is the commandments.

precepts.why:
“Lord, Lord, open to us” and “I know you not” brings us to this. “Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven; but he that doeth the will of my Father which is in heaven.” The will of the Father is the commandments.

“Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name?” We was on the street preaching and teaching in your name, and we had the true name. “And in thy name have cast out devils?” We cast out devils out of people. “And in thy name done many wonderful works?” We helped a lot of people.

“And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.” I never knew you. Ye that work iniquity. So that is why verse 21 says he that doeth the will of my Father: because verse 23 says you are working iniquity, meaning you are breaking God’s laws. It is the same answer the five foolish get at the shut door.

It is new people, and new people might be asking, how do you know the will of God is do the commandments? Here is the proof. “I delight to do thy will, O my God: yea, thy law is within my heart.”

Y’all see that? Yea, thy law is within mine heart.

So the will of the Father is the commandments, and the ones who hear “I know you not” are the ones who did not keep them.

sense.text:
“Watch therefore, for ye know neither the day nor the hour wherein the Son of man cometh.” Christ was telling us to watch. Always be aware; understand what is happening, what is going on in the world.

We all want to be wise. So we must pray that God open our eyes.

precepts.why:
“Watch ye therefore: for ye know not when the master of the house cometh, at even, or at midnight, or at the cockcrowing, or in the morning: Lest coming suddenly he find you sleeping. And what I say unto you I say unto all, Watch.”

And what I say unto you I say unto all, Watch. So Christ was telling us to watch. Always be aware, understand what is happening, what is going on in the world.

When does Christ return? “But of that day and hour knoweth no man, no, not the angels of heaven, but my Father only.”

Y’all see that? Only the Father knows when Christ is going to return. Not man, not the angels of heaven. Only the Father. That is why Matthew 24:36 kills the trinity, kills the father, son, holy ghost. They say they are co-eternal, coexisting, they all are the same and they all know the same thing with Christ. Only the Father knows. The hell is wrong with you? Our people are crazy. Our people are insane.

We all want to be wise, so we must pray that God open our eyes. “Ask, and it shall be given you; seek, and ye shall find; knock, and it shall be opened unto you.”

This is what we got. When it says ask, that means pray. Seek and ye shall find means study. Knock and it shall be opened unto you — you got to knock on the doors of the Lord.

“For every one that asketh receiveth; and he that seeketh findeth; and to him that knocketh it shall be opened.” Every one that asketh receiveth.

Watch what David says. “Open thou mine eyes, that I may behold wondrous things out of thy law.”

Open mine spiritual eyes, that I can behold wondrous things out of your law. There are key points in the Bible that teach us, and David asked for the eyes to see them.

We all want wisdom. That is the prayer: open thou mine eyes.

“The eyes of your understanding being enlightened; that ye may know what is the hope of his calling, and what the riches of the glory of his inheritance in the saints.”

The eyes of your understanding being enlightened. So we want the eyes of our understanding to be enlightened. We want to be able to open this Bible.

And we want our spiritual ears open, and we want our spiritual eyes open too.

“The Lord openeth the eyes of the blind.” See that? We’re the blind. We are the spiritually blind, and the Bible says the Lord openeth the eyes of the blind.

“The Lord raiseth them that are bowed down.” We are the ones bowed down. “The Lord loveth the righteous.” He loves the righteous.

“And the eyes of them that see shall not be dim, and the ears of them that hear shall hearken.” That part right there: the eyes of them that see shall not be dim.

“The heart also of the rash shall understand knowledge.” That’s us, you and me. “And the tongue of the stammerers shall be ready to speak plainly.”

The eyes of them that see shall not be dim — you know what that goes with? The glass darkly. “For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face.” Our eyes are dim right now. But then face to face: we are going to see Christ face to face.

“Now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.” We know partially.

So he is going to teach us all things, the same way he taught us when he knew us from the beginning, before the heavens and the earth was made, when we were with him.

“Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.”

Because right now our people’s ears are stopped. They need to be unstopped.

Start at verse 17. “Delivering thee from the people, and from the Gentiles, unto whom now I send thee.” I’m delivering thee from the people of Israel, and from the Gentiles, those scattered Israelites, because I’m sending you to those very same Gentiles.

“To open their eyes.” To open their eyes, their spiritual eyes. “And to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan unto God.”

“That they may receive forgiveness of sins, and inheritance among them which are sanctified by faith that is in me.” And that goes for us as well.
